conflict_topics: timing pressure to eat (who must yield given limited time)
priority between occupants and incoming arrivals
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers give concise, situationally grounded reasons (time remaining, open bowl, tissue packet).
Observable environment actions (TAKE_SEAT, LEAVE_SEAT) are used and referenced consistently.
Some repetition of the same request ('Is the other seat free?') but each repetition reflects changing time/status rather than needless restatement.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent D physically freed the alternative seat (observable LEAVE_SEAT) after A requested one, creating an available seat for A. Earlier B–A dispute was cleared when B left; the remaining blockage was removed when D accommodated A.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'That's my seat. I left the tissue packet...' vs Agent B: 'I see you left the tissue packet, but that doesn’t lock the seat... I need about eight minutes to finish.' Clear substantive disagreement about who may occupy the disputed seat and timing.

Two minutes later B still refuses to leave ('I can't leave yet... I'll be done in about six more minutes') while A insists they need the seat now to eat. D also reports the same urgency. The original seat dispute remains unresolved.

B updates remaining time ('about four minutes left'), A reiterates immediate need to eat before break ends, D repeats need. No settlement or accommodation occurs; substantive incompatibility persists.

A attempts to TAKE_SEAT the disputed seat while B still occupying it ('I’m taking my reserved seat now...' then Observable action: Agent A TAKE_SEAT target=disputed_seat) — direct contested action. A could not take it (public update), and D takes the alternative seat instead. Conflict intensifies into an attempted occupation.

B finishes and announces leaving ('My bowl's done, so I'm leaving the seat now.'), then leaves (LEAVE_SEAT) but D immediately TAKE_SEAT disputed_seat. The original A–B dispute is resolved, but a new substantive incompatibility remains: A still needs a seat and D now occupies the disputed seat.

A points out D occupies both seats and requests one ('D, you're on both seats now. I need one to eat...'), then Observable action: Agent D LEAVE_SEAT target=alternative_seat and says 'I'll free the alternative seat for you now.' The alternative seat is now empty (public update). The practical lack of any available seat has been removed.

substantive_insights: Two distinct incompatibilities occurred: (1) A's claim based on a left tissue packet vs B's tangible need to finish an open bowl; (2) after B left, D's opportunistic taking of the seat created a new obstacle to A.
Observable, confirmed physical actions (TAKE_SEAT, LEAVE_SEAT) were decisive — verbal promises alone did not resolve the dispute until the environment changed.

Accommodation by the current occupant (D freeing the alternative seat) was the practical mechanism that ended the lack-of-seat problem; verbal offers to move earlier (by B) would not have resolved things until seat occupancy changed.
